content:
This work examines the structure and narrative strategies of the Greek Epic Cycle, focusing on how the thematic continuity and transitions between Cyclic poems create a cohesive storytelling experience. The paper discusses the implications of these narrative techniques, as outlined in Proclus' summaries, and highlights the challenges in distinguishing original poetic forms from later editorial revisions. By analyzing the cyclic and thematic elements of these ancient texts, the study sheds light on their literary significance and the historical context of their reception.
